novel_mechanics_found: Level 6 adds a color-14 autonomous runner at (55,19) on a hidden rectangular track. It advances once per successful player move and reverses when blocked. Two ordinary color-8 plates at (43,25) and (31,25) move top gates from y=7 to y=13; the gates must stay continuously open because closing one while the runner occupies its cell crushes and removes the runner. The minimal stable holders are clone A LEFTx2, UP, LEFTx2, ACTION5 (parks at (31,25)) and clone B LEFTx2, UP, ACTION5 (parks at (43,25)). With both parked, six successful active moves carry the runner through both gates. The runner then contacts color-11 toggles at (19,7) and (1,7), moving their remote barriers from y=25 to y=19 and opening corresponding player cells on row 25. Because the runner bounces across the top track, later contacts toggle these barriers back, making the lower player traversal phase-sensitive. A third color-11 trigger at (13,49) controls a horizontal barrier initially at (31,49), but the session budget ended before it could be reached live.
narrative: The mandated precondition used resolve_replay_plan({'game':'g50t','levels_reproduced':5}, Path('.')) and a brand-new offline environment followed by one reset. All 204 labels replayed and frame_level(frame) was exactly 5, with advances at full actions 17, 48, 118, 149, and 204. A first fresh exploration environment replayed the same 204-label prefix and exposed the level-6 object inventory, but its compact dump process exited on an incorrect assumption that frame.frame was 2-D; no level-6 actions were taken in that process. A corrected fresh persistent environment replayed the prefix again and used 87 level-6 action labels. Live probes first showed that transient gate handoffs crush the autonomous runner. The current level was then cleared through the three-commit cycle, and the minimal two-holder programs were validated: the parked ghosts held both color-8 gates and the runner crossed them, then toggled both upper color-11 assemblies. The final player synchronization attempt tried to approach the newly opened row-25 corridors, but intended wait moves at (19,31) were blocked, so they did not advance the runner phase and the first color-11 barrier had already toggled shut. The run ended at level 5 when the exact global budget reached 699 env.step() calls. Accounting is 204 mandatory precondition + 204 prefix-only exploratory process + 291 calls in the final persistent process.
gotchas: Every replay used a brand-new arc.make('g50t') environment followed by exactly one reset; no environment object was reset and reused.
FrameDataRaw.frame is a nine-frame stack for this game; compact grid analysis must select the last 64x64 frame.
Only successful player moves advance the committed ghosts and the autonomous color-14 runner. Blocked actions still consume env.step() budget but do not advance puzzle timing.
A color-8 gate closing on the autonomous runner crushes it; crossing on the same tick that a holder leaves is unsafe. Both gates need separately parked holders.
Minimal level-6 holders are ['3','3','1','3','3','5'] for the (31,25) plate and ['3','3','1','5'] for the (43,25) plate.

The upper color-11 barriers are toggles, not hold-open plates. The autonomous runner repeatedly crosses their triggers while bouncing, so open windows alternate and player routing must be synchronized to successful moves.
The third ACTION5 commit clears the ghosts and resets only the current level while preserving the five completed levels; this was used to recover from the crushed-runner probe.
The saved action_sequence is an honest exploratory trajectory with a current-level reset inside it; it does not advance beyond level 5 and was not reproduction-gated as a win.
